text:
nina: quick FYI - ran a scheduled restore smoke for weekly DB snapshot and saw kms:Decrypt denied for 5 blobs. looks like backup pipeline can't decrypt older snapshots. starting triage.

rahul: which bucket/prefix? any pattern on object metadata?

nina: s3://archive-backups/db-weekly/2026-03-14/*.snap. head-object shows a key alias in metadata that doesn't match the currently-active CMK for backups.

clara: paste head-object output for one of the failing snaps pls.

nina: here

```
$ aws s3api head-object --bucket archive-backups --key db-weekly/2026-03-14/snap-batch7.snap
{
  "ContentLength": 104857600,
  "Metadata": {
    "x-amz-meta-kms-alias": "alias/redwood-backups-v1",
    "x-amz-meta-cipher": "aes-gcm-v1",
    "x-amz-meta-uploader": "backup-agent-1"
  }
}
```

nina: restore log:

```
[2026-03-22T09:12:11Z] ERROR restore: decryption failed: KMS AccessDeniedException: caller arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/backup-service-role/session does not have kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/fe12-aaaa-2222
```

rahul: hm the metadata points to alias/redwood-backups-v1. our key rotation job replaced that alias to point to new key fe12-cccc-3333 yesterday during maintenance. older objects still expecting the old key id. if the old CMK's key policy was tightened in the RBAC cleanup, that could explain denies.

clara: check CloudTrail for KMS:Decrypt calls around restore time and also for UpdateAlias operations in the last 48h.

rahul: CloudTrail shows UpdateAlias for alias/redwood-backups-v1 at 2026-03-21T23:58Z. also multiple Decrypt failures at 2026-03-22T09:12Z for principal backup-service-role. no successful decrypts for those object request ids.

incidents: tagging incident-team - partial restore impact to canary/staging. severity low-med.

nina: immediate plan I propose:
1) temporarily create a KMS grant allowing backup-service-role to Decrypt on the old key id (ttl 4h).
2) run restores for affected batches and verify.
3) audit alias -> key mappings and add a retro-compatible key-policy that permits our uploader principal to decrypt legacy snapshots.
4) add a migration job to re-encrypt old snapshots with the new key (or annotate objects with explicit key id if supported).

clara: +1 to grant. prefer CreateGrant with constraints on EncryptionContext (purpose=backup, env=staging/prod) to limit scope. avoid broad IAM policy changes.

rahul: added CreateGrant g-1b2c3d4e with limit 4h. re-run succeeded for snap-batch7. got restored to staging.

nina: nice. root cause so far: alias rotation + key-policy harden during RBAC cleanup removed decrypt permission for the uploader on the old CMK. terraform change PR#4890 tightened key policy and we missed adding a legacy exception.

clara: long-term remediation list:
- add CI that validates alias rotations: any UpdateAlias must ensure old key stays decryptable by backup principal until migration completed.
- build a migration tool to re-wrap objects (SSE-C/SSE-KMS rewrap) or copy/rewrap to new key.
- maintain mapping table (object prefix -> key id) in metadata DB for older uploads.
- add CloudWatch alarm on spikes of KMS AccessDenied for backup principals.

rahul: also add a Terraform policy guard so key-policy modifications to backup keys require a review checklist (include migration strategy).

incidents: will create incident ticket and assign postmortem owner.

nina: I'll run a full scan of the 30-day window and produce a list of affected objects and owners. ETA 3 hours.

clara: also check the restore runtime supports both cipher versions; if not, add compatibility shim or fail early at upload time. we saw some snaps using aes-gcm-v1 vs aes-gcm-v2.

rahul: logged follow-ups: TICKET-1024 (migration tool), TICKET-1025 (terraform guardrail), TICKET-1026 (CI alias-check).

nina: thanks team. once scan done I'll drop results into #postmortems and link the CreateGrant id and CloudTrail request ids. ops-bot: please note incident created. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident recorded: INC-2026-0422-restore-kms-drift. runbook reference: /docs/encops/kms-rotation-and-backup-compat.md

nina: resolved for now via grant. marking triage closed until migration plan is in place.
